LESSON: READING 15.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.2: Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade two General.

Key inquiry question: How can we know the meanings of new words in a story? 2. Why is it important to know where the events in a story happen?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination –as learner makes predictions about the story

• Critical thinking and problem solving –as learner answers indirect questions

Values:
Love as learner reads materials about caring for others.

Link to Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Citizenship Education (Child care and protection)-as learner reads texts related to the theme.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Comprehension skills are necessary in all learning areas

Suggested Learning Resources:

Pictures, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted digital devices

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
